newsitem.title: USA: Time has "conceptual" pact to cut debt - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Time has "conceptual" pact to cut debt - WSJ.

text.p: Time Warner Inc said it has a "conceptual understanding" with entertainment partner U S West Inc for a restructuring that would let Time Warner cut its cable holdings and its debt, the Wall Street Journal said Wednesday.

The paper, citing people familiar with the talks, said the pact calls for U S West to exchange its holding in Time Warner's movie studio and HBO for about four million cable subscribers. The move would give U S West several million dollars worth of Time warner debt, the paper said.
"This is a tremendously complicated structure," Time Warner President Richard Parsons told the paper, adding that there are many issues to be resolved.
The paper said the companies are still negotiating over the value and location of the cable systems that U S West would receive. It added that Time Warner executives say no deal is imminent.
On Tuesday Time Warner reported strong fourth-quarter earnings and nominated executive Stephen Bollenbach, Hilton Hotels' chief executive, and UAL Corp Chairman Gerald Greewald to its board.
Analysts applauded the nominations as steps toward increasing shareholder value.
Time Warner shares closed Tuesday up 1-7/8 at 41-1/2.
